title: Bethel Christian ave., Laurel Hill Historic District
summary: The Bethel-Christian Avenue-Laurel Hill Historic District preserves a living neighborhood shaped by Setalcott and African American families, community institutions and efforts to keep their history visible.
listing_image_alt: Bethel AME Historic District Setauket Christian Ave_5I5A0274 WEB
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Setauket Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Established in 2005, this half-mile historic district preserves the Bethel AME Church, Laurel Hill Cemetery, and the homes of tightly knit families of mixed Native American and African American descent. Acknowledging these shared neighborhoods challenges the harmful myth of Native disappearance, illustrating how Indigenous people adapted, intermarried, and built enduring institutions to survive centuries of marginalization.
history_content:
The district’s history includes Native and African American families whose relationships cannot be reduced to a single census label. Community historians connect family memory with the wider history of Setauket.

Family knowledge in public history

Theodore Green helped document this community’s past. Today, Helen Sells contributes to public interpretation, while Kevin Sells’s recorded recollections connect family reunions with the museum’s Chicken Hill exhibition.12

Follow the broader story in Setauket Ancestral Land.
preservation_content: Residents continue to make their lives here. Enjoy the district from public roads and paths, attend announced community events, and respect homes and places of worship. Historic interest does not grant access to private property.
